name: MYOTONIC DYSTROPHY TYPE I AND II

data.value:
Indication: ? Myotonic dystrophy type 1

TEST DESCRIPTION

Myotonic Dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is a multisystem disorder that affects skeletal and smooth muscle as well sas the eye, heart, endocrine system, and central nervous system. The clinical findings, which span a continuum from mild to severe, have been categorized into three somewhat overlapping phenotypes: mild, classic, and congenital. DM1 is caused by expansion of CTG trinucleotide repeat in the non-coding region of the DMPK gene. The diagnosis of DM1 is  suspected in individuals with characteristic muscle weakness and is confirmed by molecular genetic testing of DMPK. CTG repeat length exceeding 34 repeats is abnormal. Molecular genetic testing detects pathogenic variants in nearly 100% of affected individuals. 

METHODOLOGY

Triplet primed PCR (TP-PCR) and Sanger Sequence

RESULTS

Myotonic Dystrophy type 1 (DM1) – DMPK
Number of CTG repeats
Upper allele 27
Lower allele 13

INTERPRETATION

  • This individuals shows absence of expanded CTG repeat tract (Upper ~ 27 repeats and Lower ~13 repeats) at the DMPK locus (Normal range 05-49 repeats) (GeneReviews).
  • This individuals is highly unlikely to be affected with Myotonic Dystrophy Type I.
Number of CTG repeats  Allele Description
5-34 CTG repeats Normal allele
35-49 CTG repeats Mutable normal (premutation) alleles – Individuals with CTG expansions in the premutation range have not been reported to have symptoms, but their children are at increased risk of inheriting a larger repeat size and thus having symptoms.
>50 CTG repeats Full-penetrance alleles – Full-penetrance alleles are associated with disease manifestations

RECOMMENDATION

  • These results must be interpreted in the context of this individual’s clinical profile.
  • Genetic counseling is recommended.

 

 

Indication: ? Myotonic dystrophy type 2

TEST DESCRIPTION

Myotonic Dystrophy type 2 (DM2) is an automosomal dominant multisystem disorder that causes muscle pain and stiffness, progressive muscle weakness, myotonia, male hypogonadism, cardiac arrhythmias, diabetes, and early cataracts. Other features may include cognitive dysfunction, hypersommnia, tremor, and hearling loss. DM2 is caused by expansion of a CCTG tetranucleotide repeat in intron 1 of the CNBP gene. Normal CNBP alleles have up to    30 repeats whereas pathogenic alleles contain from 75 to 11,000 repeats.

METHODOLOGY

Triplet primed PCR (TP-PCR) and Sanger Sequence

RESULTS

Myotonic Dystrophy type 2 (DM2) – CNBP
Number of CCTG repeats
Upper allele 49
Lower allele 22

INTERPRETATION

  • This individuals shows the CCTG repeat length in one alleles (Upper repeats: ~49) at the CNBP locus to be within the mutable normal/premutation range (30-54 repeats) (GeneReviews).
  • Clinical correlation is advised.
Number of CCTG repeats  Allele Description
5-34 CTG repeats Normal allele
~30-~54 CCTG repeats Mutable normal (premutation) alleles
~55-74 CCTG repeats Unknown significance (premutation vs pathogenic)
~75-11,000 CCTG repeats Pathogenic

RECOMMENDATION

  • These results must be interpreted in the context of this individual’s clinical profile.
  • Genetic counseling is recommended.

LIMITATIONS

  • Diagnostic errors can occur due to rare sequence variations.
  • Although all precautions are taken during molecular genetic testing the currently available data indicate that the technical error rate for all types of Molecular DNA analysis is approximately 1%.
